## What Marathon is

Marathon is a sci-fi survival extraction first-person shooter from the creators of Halo and Destiny.{{cite:marathon-official-site}} Players scavenge the lost colony of Tau Ceti IV for valuables while facing UESC security, rival players, and hazardous environments.{{cite:bungie-press-mid-season-2}} Runners inhabit moddable biosynthetic bodies called Runner shells tied to distinct gameplay archetypes.{{cite:bungie-runner-shells}}

## Release, platforms, and editions

Marathon officially launched on March 5, 2026.{{cite:bungie-server-slam}} Marathon is sold in Standard and Deluxe editions across supported platforms.{{cite:bungie-press-symbiosis}}

## Price and purchase

Pre-orders offered additional in-game rewards and platform-specific bonuses like PS5 PlayStation Plus weapon charms.{{cite:bungie-server-slam}}

## Core loop and live service

Seasons last about three months and deliver free content updates including new zones, shells, and gameplay features.{{cite:bungie-introducing-seasons}} Bungie added a permanent cooperative PvE roguelite mode named Expedition in a November 2026 update.{{cite:bungie-expedition-phase-1}}

## What Marathon is

Marathon is a sci-fi survival extraction first-person shooter from the creators of Halo and Destiny.{{cite:marathon-official-site}} Players scavenge the lost colony of Tau Ceti IV for valuables while facing UESC security, rival players, and hazardous environments.{{cite:bungie-press-mid-season-2}} Matches can include up to 16 players across the available maps and modes.{{cite:pcgamer-review}} When a Runner dies they permanently lose the loot from that run unless they successfully exfiltrate.{{cite:pcgamer-guide}} Runners inhabit moddable biosynthetic bodies called Runner shells tied to distinct gameplay archetypes.{{cite:bungie-runner-shells}} Six launch Runner shells are available at release, including the Thief shell.{{cite:bungie-introducing-seasons}}

## Release, platforms, and editions

Marathon officially launched on March 5, 2026.{{cite:bungie-server-slam}} Marathon is sold in Standard and Deluxe editions across supported platforms.{{cite:bungie-press-symbiosis}} The standard retail price at launch was set at forty US dollars.{{cite:pcgamer-guide}}

## Price and purchase

Pre-orders offered additional in-game rewards and platform-specific bonuses like PS5 PlayStation Plus weapon charms.{{cite:bungie-server-slam}} Pre-orders included in-game cosmetics, an emblem, a player background, and linked Destiny 2 rewards via Bungie.net.{{cite:bungie-server-slam}}

## Core loop and live service

Seasons last about three months and deliver free content updates including new zones, shells, and gameplay features.{{cite:bungie-introducing-seasons}} Seasonal updates are free and introduce weapons, Runner shells, zones, events, and systems that change play and progression.{{cite:bungie-introducing-seasons}} Bungie added a permanent cooperative PvE roguelite mode named Expedition in a November 2026 update.{{cite:bungie-expedition-phase-1}} In Expedition players join dedicated PvE queues to run roguelite cooperative missions across Perimeter, Night Marsh, Outpost, and Cryo Archive.{{cite:bungie-expedition-phase-1}}

## Overview

Marathon features six factions: CyberAcme, Arachne, Sekiguchi Genetics, MIDA, Traxus, and NuCaloric.{{cite:pcgamer-guide}}

## Unlocking factions and contracts

Factions become available after completing liaison contracts, which enable reputation and further contracts for that faction.{{cite:gamesradar-factions}}

## Reputation and upgrades

Completing contracts grants faction reputation used to unlock seasonal upgrades, stronger base stats, and Armory wares.{{cite:bungie-introducing-seasons}} Each season provides a clean slate with progression resets for faction ranks, while liaison contract progress carries over.{{cite:bungie-introducing-seasons}} Season 2 moved many Runner shell upgrades into the Cradle and introduced unique implant families per faction.{{cite:bungie-welcome-season-2}}

## UESC as antagonist

The derelict UESC Marathon serves as the site for end-game Cryo Archive content aboard the ship.{{cite:bungie-server-slam}} UESC combatants appear during runs and were tuned by Bungie to adjust their health and combat impact (Update 1.0.0.4, March 11, 2026).{{cite:bungie-update-1-0-0-4}}

bodyMarkdown:
## Overview

Marathon features six factions: CyberAcme, Arachne, Sekiguchi Genetics, MIDA, Traxus, and NuCaloric.{{cite:pcgamer-guide}}

## Unlocking factions and contracts

Factions become available after completing liaison contracts, which enable reputation and further contracts for that faction.{{cite:gamesradar-factions}} Liaison contracts are issued by ONI and must be completed to unlock a faction for reputation gain and full contract access.{{cite:gamesradar-factions}} Priority contracts are one-time narrative missions that offer superior rewards such as Marathon weapons, backpacks, and Salvage.{{cite:gamesradar-factions}} Standard contracts are repeatable challenges that grant reputation and basic rewards, with one active contract at a time and optional re-rolls for Credits.{{cite:gamesradar-factions}}

## Reputation and upgrades

Completing contracts grants faction reputation used to unlock seasonal upgrades, stronger base stats, and Armory wares.{{cite:bungie-introducing-seasons}} Seasonal faction upgrades provide passive perks like stronger starting loadouts, expanded vault space, and specialized Armory wares.{{cite:marathon-official-site}} Each season provides a clean slate with progression resets for faction ranks, while liaison contract progress carries over.{{cite:bungie-introducing-seasons}} Season 2 moved many Runner shell upgrades into the Cradle and introduced unique implant families per faction.{{cite:bungie-welcome-season-2}} Season 2 introduced the Cradle system, moving many Runner shell upgrades out of faction trees and adding unique head, torso, and leg implant families per faction.{{cite:bungie-welcome-season-2}}

## UESC as antagonist

The derelict UESC Marathon serves as the site for end-game Cryo Archive content aboard the ship.{{cite:bungie-server-slam}} The Cryo Archive, aboard the derelict UESC Marathon, is an end-game zone that unlocks during Season 1.{{cite:bungie-server-slam}} UESC combatants appear during runs and were tuned by Bungie to adjust their health and combat impact (Update 1.0.0.4, March 11, 2026).{{cite:bungie-update-1-0-0-4}} Update 1.0.0.4 (March 11, 2026) reduced most UESC enemy health by about 10–15% and UESC boss shield HP by 25%.{{cite:bungie-update-1-0-0-4}}

title: Runner shells
summary: Overview of Marathon's Runner shells, how cores and implants differ, the roster across seasons, and former codenames.
bodyMarkdown:
## What Runner shells are

Runner shells are moddable biosynthetic bodies that house player consciousness for survival on Tau Ceti.{{cite:bungie-runner-shells}} Runner shells provide diverse playstyle foundations for scavenging moddable weapons, implants, and core upgrades.{{cite:marathon-official-site}} Rook is a frame designed for scavenger mode, letting a solo player join in-progress matches without risking a loadout.{{cite:bungie-runner-shells}}

## Cores versus implants

Cores are generally tied to one specific Runner shell and modify how that shell’s abilities function.{{cite:bungie-runner-shells}} Implants are universal across Runner shells and provide stats plus a random perk, with high-tier implants granting a bonus fixed perk.{{cite:bungie-runner-shells}} Season 2 changed implants to be defined by perk first and have fixed stats, with names reflecting their perks.{{cite:bungie-welcome-season-2}}

## Roster and seasons

Bungie announced Sentinel as a new Season 2 Runner shell built for area control and defensive play.{{cite:bungie-welcome-season-2}} Bungie announced Bishop as a new Runner shell arriving with the Symbiosis update, focused on fast, surgical melee bursts.{{cite:bungie-nightfall-refresh}}

## Former codenames

Community sources list Thief, Triage, Vandal, Recon, Assassin, Destroyer, and Rook with former or informal codenames Glitch, Blackbird, Void, Locus, and others.{{cite:marathonwiki-org-runners}}

title: Weapons
summary: This page covers Marathon's launch weapons by class and ammo type, general weapon systems, ammo economy, and post-launch weapon additions and balance changes.
bodyMarkdown:
## Overview

Marathon launched with 28 weapons and a full complement of mods, implants, and cores.{{cite:bungie-introducing-seasons}} Launch weapons span standard categories including assault rifles, shotguns, SMGs, precision rifles, machine guns, railguns, sniper rifles, and pistols.{{cite:gamesradar-weapons}}

## How weapons, loot, and ammo work

Factions and Armory offerings can grant weapons, weapon chip mods, and other rank-up rewards.{{cite:gamesradar-factions}} Some high-power ammo categories are rarer and have smaller stack sizes, making them more costly to use.{{cite:pcgamer-review}}

## Post-launch weapons and tuning

The KKV-9SD is a very fast-fire pistol-frame SMG with an integrated suppressor and folding stock mod compatibility.{{cite:bungie-welcome-season-2}} The D54 Battle Pistol is a full-auto, three-round-burst handgun designed to bridge pistol and magnum archetypes and uses folding stock mods.{{cite:bungie-s2-combat-tuning}} Season 2 reworked ammo economy, range identities, and weapon roles to make choices clearer and archetypes distinct.{{cite:bungie-s2-combat-tuning}} Mid‑Season 2 balance updates included WSTR Combat Shotgun buffs and balance changes to the D54 Battle Pistol and Misriah-2442 shotgun.{{cite:bungie-press-mid-season-2}} Update 1.1.0.1 (June 9, 2026) fixed issues including an interaction with the D54 Battle Pistol's Daredevil Stock Prestige mod.{{cite:bungie-update-1-1-0-1}} A later content update announced new weapons: the V17 Flamethrower and the Maverick revolver-style weapon.{{cite:bungie-press-symbiosis}}

summary: This page explains the extraction loop in Marathon: infil, scavenging, PvPvE encounters, exfil, death penalties, solo versus crew options, and the Vault system.
bodyMarkdown:
## Overview of a run

Runs take place on Tau Ceti IV and include scavenging, combat, and exfiltration phases.{{cite:marathon-official-site}} Matches are survival extraction encounters featuring both PvP and PvPvE elements.{{cite:marathon-official-site}}

## Infil and loot

Players infil into zones like Perimeter, Dire Marsh, Outpost, and Cryo Archive.{{cite:bungie-vidoc}} Scavenging yields moddable weapons, implants, and core system upgrades for builds.{{cite:marathon-official-site}} Certain high-value loot like Tag Chips count toward Ranked score targets.{{cite:bungie-ranked}}

## PvPvE, death, and penalties

When a runner dies, they lose all carried loot and cannot retrieve it.{{cite:pcgamer-guide}} In Ranked, failing to exfil or dying causes loss of Ranked Points based on Holotag values.{{cite:bungie-ranked}} Holotags set a score target and a loss penalty for a team's run.{{cite:bungie-ranked}}

## Exfil, crews, solo play, and Vaults

Exfil rewards stronger builds by allowing players to keep stolen loot and advance progression.{{cite:marathon-official-site}} The Vault Breaker mode lets players attempt Cryo Archive content solo, in duos, or in trios.{{cite:bungie-press-mid-season-2}}
